item.title: Zod Brings In-Process Schema Compilation and a 9x Cut in Memory Footprint
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/zod-schema-compliation/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792163115814.jpg"/><p>Zod is a TypeScript-focused schema validation library that recently released versions 4.5 and 4.6. Key updates include schema compilation for faster data parsing, significant memory usage reductions, and new validation features. The library supports efficient validation processes and remains popular in the JavaScript ecosystem, achieving millions of downloads weekly.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Uber Automates Dependency Analysis Across Its Service Mesh
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/uber-automated-dependency/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791060253143.jpg"/><p>Uber has developed an automated dependency analysis system that uses RPC middleware and production metrics to correlate caller and downstream failures. The approach classifies dependencies as fail-close, fail-open, or unknown and addresses limitations of sampled distributed tracing for rare failures across Uber’s large service mesh.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: AI in Production: Panellists Highlight Silent Failures, Harness Engineering, and Agent Governance
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ai-systems-production/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792118181680.jpg"/><p>A recent InfoQ webinar examined operational challenges in deploying agentic systems. Key points included issues like semantic and embedding drift, which can lead to significant errors. Experts discussed the need for automated code reviews, continuous evaluation of models, and enhanced privacy measures. The session emphasised a strategic approach to deployment and security management.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

item.title: Mini book: Evolutionary Architecture in Practice
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/minibooks/evolutionary-architecture/en/smallimage/thumb-1791282847807.jpg"/><p>Discover how to keep software evolvable as systems, technology, and teams shift. This edition explores agentic fitness functions for semantic drift, treating human comprehension as a core design metric, cross-cloud guardrails for regional autonomy, and aligning technical boundaries with Conway’s Law. Move beyond static diagrams to continuous feedback systems that keep change safe and intentional.</p> <i>By InfoQ</i>

item.title: Helidon 27 Introduces Restructured Programming Models and New Messaging and Data Modules
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/helidon-27-released/en/headerimage/java-istock-image-01-1792149493797.jpg"/><p>The release of Helidon 27 is the first release that follows the Oracle Tip & Tail Model of Library Development by which the Tip adopts the latest Java technology while the Tail provides a more stable and secure baseline. Concurrent with the release of JDK 27, new features in Helidon 27 include: an introduction to new major modules, Helidon Messaging and Helidon Data JDBC.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

item.title: Presentation: Exploding GPUs
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/ai-security-kubernetes-gpu-threats/en/mediumimage/andrew-martin-medium-1790846331295.jpeg"/><p>Andrew Martin discusses why AI security is fundamentally tied to Kubernetes security. He shares insights into the evolving AI threat landscape, covering non-deterministic agent behavior, GPU supply chain vulnerabilities, shared compute risks, and practical defense strategies - from prompt firewalling to agentic identity - to help secure cloud-native AI workloads in production environments.</p> <i>By Andrew Martin</i>

item.title: AWS Introduces Strands Decider 2B and Strands Box for AI Agent Development
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/aws-strands-agents/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792079603910.jpg"/><p>AWS has introduced two open-source projects for AI agent development: Strands Decider 2B, a small model designed to make decisions within agent workflows, and Strands Box, a sandbox for controlling agent execution. Both projects address different aspects of building agents that use tools, execute code, and interact with external systems.</p> <i>By Daniel Dominguez</i>

item.title: Article: Cryptographic Foundation of Mobile ID Systems: An ISO/IEC 18013-5 Enterprise Architecture Blueprint
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/enterprise-mobile-id-mdl-blueprint/en/headerimage/enterprise-mobile-id-mdl-blueprint-header-1791967143918.jpg"/><p>This article provides a framework for asking the right architectural questions before an enterprise commits to an mDL provider or library. It shows which components can be abstracted safely, which trust boundaries must remain visible to the enterprise, what cryptographic and interoperability properties should be verified, and how requirements change across real-world use cases.</p> <i>By Praveen Kumar Gopalakrishnan</i>

item.title: Chainguard Launches Secure Workspaces and Checks for AI Coding Agents
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/chainguard-workspaces-checks/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792079610138.jpg"/><p>Software supply chain security company Chainguard has announced two beta products for running and testing code written by developers and AI agents. Chainguard Workspaces provides remote development environments based on hardened microVMs, while Chainguard Checks moves continuous integration into the development loop. The company announced both products at its Assemble London event.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: Microsoft Commits Maia to Multi-Gigawatt Inference, and Its Efficiency Metric Draws Questions
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/azure-maia-300/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791943943820.jpg"/><p>Microsoft will scale its Maia accelerator family to multi-gigawatt deployments from 2027, making it the primary inference system for its own products. Maia 300 collapses scale-up and scale-out onto one Ethernet fabric and moves KV state between prefill and decode workers without leaving it. Practitioners have questioned the tokens-per-watt claim that leads the announcement.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Instagram Modernized its UI with an AI-Native Architecture, Cutting Token Costs by 33%
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/instagram-compose-migration/en/headerimage/aws-reliability-dns-1792077775251.jpg"/><p>Instagram Direct migrated its Android UI from the legacy Android View system to Jetpack Compose, creating an AI-native UI codebase that is easier for AI coding agents to understand, modify, and maintain. According to Instagram engineers, the migration reduced UI code volume by 50% and token costs per AI agent session by 33%.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Optimizing Software Workflow: Exploring Fundamental Impacts in Technology
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/optimize-software-workflow/en/headerimage/header-1791282094936.jpg"/><p>Software only has value when shipped; faster release cadence matters. Development, deployment, and operations require different thinking, metrics, and investments. There are four impacts in tech: product success, compute capacity, engineering capacity, and strategic innovation. The biggest expense is people. AI shifts engineers toward deeper problem understanding, not fewer engineers.</p> <i>By Ben Linders</i>

item.title: Presentation: What 25 Trillion Tokens Reveal About How Developers Actually Adopt AI Agents
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/agentic-ai-developer-trust-adoption/en/mediumimage/brendan-oleary-medium-1791452159106.jpeg"/><p>Brendan O'Leary discusses how real-world AI adoption depends on building trust rather than chasing model benchmarks. Drawing from 40 trillion tokens of usage data, he explains the four rungs of the AI adoption ladder and analyzes key failure points in context construction, multi-model routing, and feedback loops to help engineering leaders successfully scale agentic workflows.</p> <i>By Brendan O’Leary</i>

item.title: Grafana Tempo 3.1 Adds Query-Based Trace Redaction and Sampling-Aware TraceQL Metrics
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/grafana-tempo-31/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791965478500.jpg"/><p>Grafana Labs has released Tempo 3.1, the first minor update to the 3.0 architecture. It adds TLS and additional SASL mechanisms to the Kafka client, lets operators redact traces with a TraceQL query instead of a list of trace IDs, and introduces an experimental query-time hint that corrects TraceQL metrics for sampled data.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

item.title: Cloudflares Newly Acquired Vite+ Reaches 1.0 with GitLab CI Support, Hooks, and tsup Migration
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-viteplus-stable/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791892196672.jpg"/><p>VoidZero has launched Vite+ 1.0, the first stable version of its JavaScript toolchain. It features a command line tool for managing Node.js, package management, and frontend development from a single configuration file. Enhancements include CI integration for GitLab and Docker support. Future updates are planned, focusing on stability and diagnostics.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Backstage 1.55 Adds Scaffolder Task Recovery and Removes Deprecated Catalog APIs
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/backstage-1-55-task-recovery/en/headerimage/header-1791490255579.jpeg"/><p>Backstage 1.55 adds opt-in recovery for Software Template tasks, resuming crashed or timed-out runs from the last completed step. The release also carries breaking changes to the catalog, search and TechDocs, so teams should review their configuration before upgrading to the current 1.55.3 patch.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

item.title: ZCS Command Injection via SNMP Handlers Enables Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/zimbra-command-injection/en/headerimage/headerZimbra-1791879318550.jpg"/><p>A critical remote command execution vulnerability in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite, identified as CVE-2026-73570, poses risks by allowing unauthorized access to mailbox data and credentials. This flaw, stemming from improper input sanitization, has been actively exploited. Organizations are advised to upgrade to version 10.1.20 or disable susceptible SNMP services to mitigate risks.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

item.title: AWS Reworks EventBridge Custom Buses for Enterprise-Scale Event-Driven Architectures
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/aws-eventbridge-scaling/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791474735792.jpg"/><p>AWS has introduced an enhanced Custom Event Bus for Amazon EventBridge, targeting a problem that often emerges when event-driven architectures move beyond a single team or AWS account: the event infrastructure itself becomes fragmented.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: Presentation: How Eve Online Leverages Head Based Sampling to Observe "Fun"
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/eve-observability-head-sampling/en/mediumimage/nicholas-herring-medium-1791444748399.jpg"/><p>Nicholas Herring shares how EVE Online tackles distributed tracing and observability across a 20-year-old MMO architecture. He discusses leveraging head-based, dynamic exponential moving average (EMA), and deterministic sampling techniques to maintain high system fidelity, control telemetry costs, and avoid performance degradation under high-throughput real-time game simulations.</p> <i>By Nicholas Herring</i>

item.title: Cloudflare’s OHTTP Gateway Refuses to Decrypt Requests That Arrive through Cloudflare
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-ohttp-gateway/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791773464365.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has opened a closed beta of its OHTTP Gateway, a managed endpoint that decrypts Oblivious HTTP requests for an origin. The design choice drawing attention is a refusal: the Gateway will not decrypt requests arriving from Cloudflare Workers or from hosts proxied through Cloudflare, because that would put client identifiers and request contents in the same hands.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Presentation: You Can't Trust Your AI Bill. And Neither Can I
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/ai-cloud-cost-economics/en/mediumimage/erik-peterson-medium-1791451373591.jpg"/><p>Erik Peterson discusses why AI spend is eclipsing cloud bills, triggering a major software engineering cost crisis. He explains tokenmaxxing, unit economics, forced developer promotions, and why fully autonomous AI will write, deploy, and govern code by 2028.</p> <i>By Erik Peterson</i>

item.title: React 19.3: Adds a browser() API, Giving Client-Only Rendering a First-Class Name
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/react-19-3-browser-api/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791791785119.jpg"/><p>React 19.3 was released on September 9, introducing several features including the react-dom browser() API. This API allows components to opt out of server-side rendering, addressing issues with components that rely on client-specific data. It provides a cleaner solution for managing hydration mismatches and supports conditional data fetching, enhancing flexibility for developers.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: GitLab 19.4 Adds Goal-Driven Agents and Tighter Cost Controls
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/gitlab-19-4-goal-driven-agents/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791743492913.jpg"/><p>GitLab has released version 19.4 of its DevSecOps platform, adding a goal-driven mode to GitLab Duo CLI, three hosted open-weight models, a larger set of Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, and more detailed controls for AI spending.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: Foresight AI Brings Gremlin Agents to Reliability Engineering
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/gremlin-foresight-ai/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791653267864.jpg"/><p>Reliability management company Gremlin has announced the general availability of Foresight AI, an agentic product that analyses services for potential failures, recommends changes and reruns tests to check that a fix works.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>
